chapter: World's Greatest Jazz Band and Denver
title: The Kansas City Hall of Fame, 1970
summary: He was the first sideman honored, called by Clark Terry, which overwhelmed him.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: Well, one thing, Gus, we didn't say. That was 1970, and you were awarded the Hall of Fame from Kansas City.
How did that come about? You weren't a Kansas City alumnus.
Well, I lived in Kansas City a long
Yes, I guess that's right, yeah.
And everyone said I'm from Kansas City.
Yeah. Was that like a civic thing? Was that the city?
Yeah, they even had Woody Herman's band there. He was the big band that was there, and they had some big bands from Kansas City, all like that.
And it was in my honor, and it surprised me.
Clark Terry is the one that called me and told me that they'd got my name for the Hall of Fame in Kansas City.
And you were the first side man so honored?
Yeah, you must have been very --
Made me choke up at the mike, to say something. It just got me.
